title: Japanese Workers Pay Services to Ask for Leave
paragraphs: In Japan, asking your boss for time off can be stressful. Now, some workers are paying professionals to ask for them.

According to reports, a growing number of people are using services that contact their company and ask for a leave of absence on their behalf. One of the companies offering this service is Kawagoe Mizuho Law, a legal office. Its service usually costs about 55,000 yen.

The service works like this. First, a representative contacts the worker's company. Then, the representative officially tells the company that the worker wants to take leave. The representative also helps with the paperwork. In many cases, the representative has several talks with the company to decide the details. This is because each company has its own rules about how long people can take leave, what documents they need, and how they can return to work.

So why do people use these services? Many workers are afraid of how their boss will react. They do not want to have a difficult or angry conversation. For some people, asking for a long leave from a strict employer can make stress, burnout or personal problems even worse. The service can make the process less emotionally difficult.
Interestingly, the service is not only used by young workers. According to the law office, it has also helped middle managers in their 50s and even government workers.

A similar trend has become popular in Japan in recent years. Some people use "resignation agencies" to tell their company that they want to quit their job. The new leave services show that many Japanese workers still find it hard to speak openly with their bosses.
Many customers believe the high price is worth it, because it lets them take a break from work without making a stressful situation even worse.
